findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the temperature-sensitive tape for the dish washer the facility uses is for 180 F, which means the water inside the dish washer is so hot that it is more steam than water when it hits the dishes. PIC states the facility normally uses a heavy wash cycle. Inspector measured the dish machine using a final temperature registering plate to be 151 F on the top rack, which is too low for sanitizing. Inspector used 160 F temperature-sensitive tape on the bottom rack which showed final temperatures of 160 F or above. PIC used 180 F temperature-sensitive tape on the bottom rack which showed final temperatures of 180 F or above. Inspector and PIC discussed using 160-170-180 F temperature-sensitive tape or a final temperature measuring plate to determine what is the optimal wash cycle and placement for dish sanitizing. Ensure that mechanical warewashing sanitizing water is between 160-170 F.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: Observed that the prep sink and 3 handwashing sinks in the classroom had low hot water pressure. PICs were notified and they discussed repairs with the custodian. Ensure that water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.12 Pressure. Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water supplied as specified under 5-104.12(A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure. [Pf]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the all gender single-use bathroom for adults did not have a lid on the trash can. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and ordered a lidded trash can that will arrive the next business day. Ensure that all bathrooms used by women have a covered trash receptacle in the stall.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No CFM is present during operation. All category II facilities must have adequate coverage.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: No FSSMC present at facility. Facility recent changed to high. 90 Day follow-up will occur.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Clean utensils are stored in a basket which has dust and crumbs in it. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Clean container and utensils and maintain clean.
